subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Which attribution fields should become stable in status/usage JSON, and what privacy policy should apply to channel target identifiers?
rationale: Current main exposes partial metadata but no single stable contract for cron job identity or channel target kind; adding fields locks a public JSON/API surface used by external dashboards.

options.title: Add stable minimal fields
options.body: Expose `sessionKind`, `cronJobId`, `cronJobName`, and `channelTargetKind`, reuse existing attribution fields, and omit raw target ids by default.

options.title: Document the current split
options.body: Keep status and usage surfaces as-is for now and document the partial `agentId`, `kind`, `channel`, `chatType`, and `origin` fields instead of expanding the schema.

options.title: Require explicit privacy opt-in
options.body: Add an explicit flag or setting before emitting any target-like identifiers beyond coarse channel classification.

recommendation.title: Add stable minimal fields
recommendation.body: Expose `sessionKind`, `cronJobId`, `cronJobName`, and `channelTargetKind`, reuse existing attribution fields, and omit raw target ids by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the permanent shared usage/status schema, and Peter Steinberger has adjacent shared usage refactor history in the affected surface.
